articles.title: NHL star Alex Ovechkin appears in campaign ad for pro-Putin United Russia party
articles.summary: Capitals star is long-time supporter of Russian leader. Ovechkin is NHL’s all-time leading goalscorer. Alex Ovechkin, the NHL’s all-time leading goalscorer, has appeared in a campaign ad for the United Russia party, which supports Vladimir Putin, as he prepares for the new hockey season.
body: The Russian business newspaper Vedomosti published images of the Washington Capitals star alongside pro-Putin figures such as Russia’s foreign minister, Sergey Lavrov, the leading parliamentary candidate on United Russia’s list, and Margarita Simonyan, the editor-in-chief of the propaganda network RT.

Ovechkin is a long-time supporter of Putin. In 2017, he launched Putin Team, a social movement that he hoped would unite “people who are proud of their country and want to make Russia stronger.” He also praised the Russian leader’s “trust in and respect for his people, his fairness [and] righteousness, and the fact that he really cares.”

The 40-year-old was more cautious about his backing of Putin after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. He said he hoped the war “was going to be over and we are going to be living in a good world”, although he still said that Putin was “my president”. Hundreds of thousands of people have been killed in the war that followed Putin’s invasion.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes triumphant on NFL return as Chiefs beat up misfiring Broncos
articles.summary: Denver Broncos 10–31 Kansas City Chiefs. Chiefs QB throws two TDs on return from torn ACL. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 173 yards on debut. Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns on his Chiefs debut, stealing some of the spotlight from Patrick Mahomes as Kansas City…
body: The big question, even after Mahomes participated in the entire offseason program and every practice of training camp, was how his surgically repaired left knee would hold up nine months to the day since he tore his ACL. He erased many of those doubts when he capped the Chiefs’ opening drive with a 15-yard touchdown run.
“You see that goalline, you’re a football player and you just try and get in the end zone,” Mahomes said after the game when asked if his time on the sidelines had made him more cautious.

Mahomes didn’t appear to be affected too badly by the knee, or the brace he wore on it, throwing for 184 yards and two scores while running for another to help the Chiefs snap a three-game skid against the Broncos, who ended Kansas City’s nine-year run as division champs last season.

Walker carried 23 times to finish with the most yards rushing by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against the Colts in 2012, the year before Andy Reid became their coach. The ex-Seahawks star also had three catches for 18 yards.

articles.title: Cost of watching sport in Australia creeps up as streaming services search for long-term viability
articles.summary: Nine and Stan lock up Premier League rights for $120m a year. Six major streamers increased base prices since February 2025. Five dollars here, three dollars there, but an increase almost everywhere.
body: The partnership now runs until 2034, and follows the Nine Entertainment group taking over the rights from now defunct Optus Sport last year. The price – reportedly around $120m per year – consolidates the Premier League’s place as the fourth most sought after sporting competition on Australian television.

These ballooning rights fees are increasingly passed on to customers as the sector seeks long-term viability. A survey of costs of Australia’s eight major sports streamers showed six have increased their base pricing since the start of 2025.

Only Disney+ – which offers ESPN – has decreased its base price over that time, but that reflects the introduction of an ad-supported tier, following a trend of subscription platforms that once heralded the lack of advertising now ramping it up.
“The price hikes go along with the cost of production and the cost of rights,” she said.

articles.title: How Maresca is tackling football's impossible job
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca seemingly took on an impossible job in the summer when replacing the legendary Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, but is making it look an easy task in the early stages of his tenure.
body: Four victories in as many games has City sitting joint-top of the Premier League alongside Arsenal, and the early signs suggest those two sides will be the ones tussling for the title once more.

Maresca clinched his most significant win since taking charge with an impressive 1-0 victory against rivals Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday, despite playing much of the game with 10 men following Phil Foden's sending-off.
The City players, though, mirrored their manager's feelings by staying calm, and it is this type of composure which has been the most impressive aspect during these first few weeks.

Maresca looked back to last September when goalkeeper Robert Sanchez was dismissed after only five minutes for former side Chelsea at the same venue - a defeat which he referenced after Sunday's game.

articles.title: Why Pietersen will add unfiltered challenge that England need - Finn
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen can be blunt and forthright and there is no better time than now to add that challenge to England's white-ball set-up, says Steven Finn.
body: I was as surprised as most that Kevin Pietersen has joined the England coaching ranks as a mentor in the build-up to the 50-over World Cup in South Africa next autumn.

Not only was his last interaction with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) sitting in the offices at Lord's being told he wouldn't play for England again in 2014, but the success of his YouTube channel, The Switch, and the time it takes to commit to something like that made it seem inconceivable that it could work.

However, when I took a step back to remember what it was like to share a dressing room with him at the beginning of my England career, I remembered a number of occasions that lead me to believe this can only be a good thing for all parties.
Kevin can be blunt and forthright, but dressing rooms need that in order to function properly. They can't be an echo chamber.

articles.title: Arsenal star misses training ahead of Carabao Cup clash with Ipswich Town
articles.summary: Ben White Injury Concern Grows Ahead of Arsenal vs Ipswich in Carabao Cup. Arsenal have a fresh problem to manage before their Carabao Cup trip to Ipswich, and it centres on Ben White.
body: White started in the 2-0 win over Sunderland at the weekend, with Mikel Arteta sticking to the same XI for a second straight Premier League match. That continuity lasted only so long. White looked uncomfortable with a groin issue late in the first half and was taken off at the break, with Jurrien Timber coming on.

There was no detailed update after the Sunderland win, but the situation has moved from minor concern to genuine doubt. White has featured in all six Arsenal matches this season, including the Community Shield victory over Manchester City, so there was already a fair argument for managing his minutes against Ipswich. Now it may not even be a choice.

If the issue is more than precautionary, Arsenal will need to decide whether to push for a return before the international break or take the obvious route and give him time. That decision could also affect any England involvement.

Arteta could at least be close to getting another defensive option back. Cristhian Mosquera, sidelined since going off against Aston Villa on August 31, is progressing. Arteta said, “He’s doing really well. Let’s see if he can get this game or the next one. It will be around that time I think.”

articles.title: 'He may well just feel at home' - how Maresca is settling in at Man City
articles.summary: The Manchester derby win is a "big feather in Enzo Maresca's cap", says former Premier League striker Chris Sutton. Manchester City beat Manchester United 1-0 on Sunday, despite going down to 10 men midway through the first half, and the victory has helped prove Maresca's tactical credentials.
body: "The most damning thing for United was that you always felt City had more control and were carrying more of a threat," Sutton told BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club.

" Iliman Ndiaye coming on for Rayan Cherki when Cherki went out on the right - I wouldn't say it was a masterstroke but it was an excellent decision because Cherki is a different type of player. Ndiaye is more of a runner, can get them up the pitch and has that threat.

"There was no doubt Manchester City supporters worried about the change from Pep [Guardiola] to Maresca but I think their recruitment has been pretty smart and pretty shrewd and I thought it was a masterclass from them.
"I'm not saying it suited them going down to 10 men, but to play as they did and look the far superior team is a big feather in Maresca's cap."

articles.title: England vs. Sri Lanka prediction, lineups, pitch report for 1st T20 as Harry Brook’s side chase more dominance
articles.summary: Sri Lanka prediction, lineups, pitch report for 1st T20 as Harry Brook’s side chase more dominance originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
body: There won't be much time for England to catch their breath before Tuesday's opener at the Utilita Bowl, and that is rather the point this September.

A 3-0 sweep of Pakistan in the Tests has barely had time to sink in before Harry Brook's side switch codes again, and they do so as clear favourites, buoyed further by a 4-0 demolition of world champions India back in July. They even have Kevin Pietersen on board as a mentor.

On the other side, Sri Lanka have not had the smoothest build-up. They lost both their warm-up fixtures against an England Lions side. And the head-to-head against England isn't great either with Sri Lanka having lost 14 of the 18 T20Is between the two sides.
Coming back to the day, Aneurin Donald gets his first England cap in place of the injured Phil Salt, walking in on the back of 489 runs and a tournament-high 37 sixes in this summer's Blast.
